clue.text: Admiralty

parts.note: the one word is read as the person who embodies the Royal Navy's top command, its senior professional officer

explanation.walkthrough: The Admiralty was the government department in charge of Britain's Royal Navy; the clue asks for the officer who stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this post was the professional head of the Board of Admiralty, the body that ran Britain's Royal Navy.

clue.text: Quarrel about nuclear pollution

definitions.meaning: to quarrel with someone is to stop being friends, a phrasal verb
the radioactive dust that settles after a nuclear blast

explanation.surface: A row breaks out about radioactive contamination.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out is to argue and part company; the same phrase as a noun names radioactive debris drifting down after an explosion.

clue.text: Landlord accommodating one investor

indicators.note: a landlord who accommodates someone gives them room inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a renter can be one who lets property out for rent
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A landlord takes in a lodger who has money to invest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentier lives on income from investments or property, so an investor living off returns fits.

clue.text: Och! Hot tea! Torture!

indicators.note: tortured words are twisted out of shape, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sips scalding tea and yelps in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torture!' sounds like the cry of the sufferer but is the anagram signal on OCH HOT TEA; the whole exclamation also describes what a bad tooth feels like when hot tea reaches it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot drinks set off a sore tooth, so the yelps and the agony together describe dental pain.

clue.text: Go in, go in for contest

definitions.meaning: to go into a room or building
to sign up for a competition

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to take part in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to step inside a place and to register as a competitor in an event.

clue.text: Fail to bring about deflation

definitions.meaning: to fail someone is to disappoint them
to release the air from a tyre or balloon

explanation.surface: An economic policy fails to reduce prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to disappoint someone, and also to let the air out of something inflatable.

clue.text: Wild rioters make merry

indicators.note: wild things are out of control, so the letters of the next word run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Unruly rioters have a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily, a synonym for reveling boisterously.

clue.text: Hare Jnr is a cad of a lad

definitions.meaning: a junior hare is a youthful animal that leaps along
a youthful scoundrel; bounder is old British slang for a cad

explanation.surface: A young rabbit-like creature is described as a disreputable youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder is dated British slang for a man who behaves dishonourably; a hare also bounds, so a young hare is literally a youthful leaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile hare is a small jumper, and a badly behaved youth is a junior scoundrel in old slang.

clue.text: A lord on form when wrestling Charles in Arden

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so these letters are moulded into another order

explanation.surface: A nobleman in good shape grapples with a man in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on form' looks like a phrase meaning fit, but 'on' is fodder and 'form' alone signals the anagram. In Shakespeare's As You Like It the hero wrestles the court wrestler Charles before fleeing to the Forest of Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's hero of As You Like It defeats the wrestler Charles and then takes refuge in the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Little birds go about a bit to find tasty little morsels

indicators.note: the two outer pieces go around the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Small birds hop around in search of crumbs to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Titbits are small choice pieces of food, delicacies in miniature.

clue.text: Vegetables environmentalists leap to support

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: to spring is to jump
Greens are members of an environmental party

explanation.surface: Ecological campaigners jump up to back a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring greens are young cabbage leaves eaten as a vegetable early in the year.

clue.text: Caveman's tool the lion chewed up

indicators.note: something chewed up is mangled, so the letters of the words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man's implement was gnawed by a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone implement from the New Stone Age, the kind of tool a prehistoric man used.

clue.text: List has nothing in it for a cocky type

indicators.note: the word for nothing is put inside the list word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names or duties
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A conceited person appears on a duty list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocky' looks like a word for arrogant, but it means a male bird here: a cock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is a male farmyard bird, the one that crows at dawn.

clue.text: He gets his teeth in with some hesitation

parts.note: a bit means some, a small amount
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone sinks their teeth in, though hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sinks teeth into things is one who bites, as a dog might.

clue.text: How to deal with an off spinner? Get away!

definitions.text: How to deal with an off spinner?
definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman may play a cut shot to an off-spin bowler and take runs

explanation.surface: Advice to a batsman facing a slow bowler, followed by a cry to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off spinner is a slow bowler who turns the ball; a cut is a shot played square, after which the batsman runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to escape hastily, and read literally describes hitting a cricket ball with a cut and running.

clue.text: Hill guide is a constant worrier

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
a mentor is a guide or adviser

explanation.surface: A mountain guide keeps fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrier' suggests someone anxious, but here it is one who worries others, harassing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor harasses and pesters others, so one who worries people relentlessly fits.

clue.text: Clothing that is not put on?

definitions.text: Clothing that is not put on?

parts.words: Clothing that is not put on?
parts.note: read 'not put on' as a garment worn beneath others rather than on top, instead of one left off

explanation.definitionFit: Garments such as pants and vests go beneath the outer clothes rather than over them.

clue.text: The TT habit of yore

definitions.meaning: two letter Ts side by side, a T written double
a garment worn in bygone times

explanation.surface: Teetotal behaviour from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: TT looks like teetotal or the Isle of Man motorcycle race, but it shows a letter T doubled. 'habit' is clothing, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of Ts makes a doubled letter, and a close-fitting Renaissance jacket for men was a garment of old.

clue.text: Column of deserters gets a foothold on the ship

indicators.note: a column of deserters puts the deserter word in front of the column word

parts.note: rats desert a sinking ship
a line is a column of people

explanation.surface: A procession of runaways gets a grip aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the rope rungs across a ship's shrouds that sailors climb, giving footing aloft.

clue.text: Twig a starting price swindle

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
to rig something is to fix it dishonestly

explanation.surface: Someone cottons on to a racecourse betting fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a verb meaning understand, but it is the noun, a small shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or stem cut from a plant.

clue.text: A scarlet woman is first to be fleeced

indicators.note: the woman word is placed at the front, before the rest

parts.note: she refers to a woman
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: An immoral woman is the first to be swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A scarlet woman' reads as one phrase for an immoral woman, but splits into A, RED and SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has been fleeced has had its wool clipped off.

clue.text: More willing to lose one's life if in rare form

indicators.note: the word for dying sits inside the rearranged letters
to form is to reshape, so the letters of the word before are put in a new order

parts.note: to die is to lose one's life

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more prepared to die if an unusual situation arises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' makes REAR from RARE, and 'in' puts DIE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, meaning more prepared or inclined.

clue.text: To act with brute resolve is not for him

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: to resolve is to break into parts and settle anew, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Acting with brute determination is not this man's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' looks like a noun for determination, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of BRUTE. The definition describes a sceptic: resolute action is not for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic hesitates and questions, so acting with firm conviction is foreign to him.

clue.text: Proper entitlement

definitions.meaning: something one has a just claim to

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means correct and fitting; the noun means a just claim such as a legal entitlement.

clue.text: Leave cryptic note to give lift

indicators.note: cryptic things are puzzling and disguised, so the letters of the word before are disguised in a new order

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a puzzling message to boost spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise up, the same as lifting.

clue.text: Making pastry thin but very rich

definitions.meaning: using a pin to flatten dough

explanation.surface: A baker flattening dough is also extremely wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin flattens pastry by this action, and the idiom 'rolling in it' means wealthy.

clue.text: Twisting hill leads leading to the holy mount

indicators.note: the hill word comes first and leads on to the mount word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
Sion, or Zion, is the holy hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A winding hill path leads up to a sacred mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, especially of a rod or wire about its axis.

clue.text: He's a business man by the way

definitions.text: He's a business man by the way

parts.words: He's a business man by the way
parts.note: 'by the way' reads as an aside but literally places the business at the roadside

explanation.definitionFit: A hawker or stallholder sells goods from the pavement or market road.
